title: sovereign-onboarding-contract-clauses-qna
content:
Purpose
This note is a working reference for Sales/Legal/Onboarding/Eng to translate customer contract clauses about data residency into concrete deployment, verification, and escalation steps. Not a legal doc — operational mapping only.

Scope
- Applies to new Private (VPC/on-prem) and Dedicated customers that request explicit region/territory commitments in contract language (e.g., data "residency", "processing in the EU", "no cross-border transfer").
- Focus on clauses that require technical enforcement rather than purely contractual representations.

High-level approach (one-liner)
Map each contract promise -> an enforcement artifact (pin config, storage scope, routing policy, telemetry evidence) + onboarding checklist + acceptance tests.

Common contract clauses we see and recommended operational mapping
1) "All customer data will be stored and processed within [REGION] and shall not be transferred outside [REGION]."
   - Enforcement artifacts: region_pin: [REGION] on customer profile; compute_wave: set compute affinity to nodes with zone tag REGION; storage_bucket: create dedicated bucket in region with residency label.
   - Runtime checks: request routing middleware asserts token.origin_region == region_pin OR rejects (403). KV-cache eviction must be region-scoped.
   - Evidence: daily audit report (signed) listing active nodes, IP ranges, and storage object locations for that account.

2) "Backups and logs will remain within [REGION] and be subject to the same residency restrictions."
   - Enforcement artifacts: backup_policy: region-only snapshot targets; logging_sink: region-limited sink + encryption key in regional KMS.
   - Operator note: we must disable global logging exports for that org; prevent routing to central analytics unless anonymized and explicitly consented.

3) "Customer data will not be accessed by staff located outside [REGION]."
   - Enforcement artifacts: admin-access-policy scoped to customer support roles filtered by geo; require Just-In-Time (JIT) access with timeboxed tickets; require session recording and customer notification for exception access.
   - Telemetry: access_audit events tagged with operator_location and justification.

4) "Where allowed, metadata necessary for routing is permitted outside region but content must stay inside."
   - Operational tradeoff: allow routing headers (region hints) to cross boundaries, but enforce transform at ingress to remove content/payload before any external transit.

Technical implementation notes (engineering-centric)
- Model serving: when a customer has a region_pin, the scheduler should mark their requests as "resident". Resident requests are eligible only on instances with residency_tag matching the pin. The scheduler must default to reject rather than fallback to non-compliant nodes unless explicit contract exception is recorded.
- KV cache and prefix caching: caches must be partitioned by region_pin. Cross-region cache sharing is forbidden for resident customers. Caching config: cache_namespace = orgID + region_pin.
- Telemetry & evidence: add fields to trace/span: residency.pin, node.region, storage.region, access.evidence_id. Audit jobs should produce a daily signed CSV for the customer and store a copy in the customer-owned regional bucket.
- Data-at-rest encryption: ensure keys are in regional KMS; do not permit use of global keys for resident buckets unless customer signs key escrow waiver.
- Network egress controls: for private deployments, add egress ACL that blocks destination CIDRs outside approved region list. For Dedicated/Hosted hybrid, enforce via NGFW + routing policies.

Onboarding checklist (pre-signature -> handoff -> go-live)
- Pre-signature:
  - Legal: capture exact wording of residency clause and list allowed exceptions.
  - Sales/SE: confirm target region(s) and expected latency SLAs.
  - Infra pre-check: capacity available in target region? Tag nodes, reserve capacity pool if needed.
- Handoff doc: include region_pin value, customer orgID, KMS preference, logging retention, allowed exceptions and escalation contacts. Attach Confluence ID.
- Provisioning:
  - Create org with region_pin and residency labels.
  - Provision storage and backups in region.
  - Provision compute pool: reserve nodes with residency_tag.
  - Configure router/policy to block non-region routes.
- Acceptance tests (pre-prod):
  - Test A: generate sample request and assert request served on node with node.region == region_pin.
  - Test B: attempt to read storage object from non-region node and expect deny.
  - Test C: run log-export job and ensure sink is regional only.
- Go-live: run 24h compliance monitor and create evidence bundle.

Edge cases and exception handling
- Grace periods for migrations: Contracts sometimes allow 90-day migration windows. Implement a timebound state: region_pin: pending-migration with explicit migration_deadline. Scheduler can service from fallback nodes while in pending state but must emit elevated telemetry and require legal sign-off.
- Shared models and global inference: For customers requiring residency but using shared model artifacts, we have two options: (1) host a cached copy of model weights in region-specific storage and run inference locally; (2) allow routed lightweight model proxy where logits are computed regionally but weight pulls happen from global store — the latter usually fails residency checks. Default: create regional model cache.
- Emergency fallback (outage): Define strict emergency policy: automatic failover to alternate region only with documented customer consent OR after N hours with exec-level sign-off. Telemetry must mark each affected request with emergency_fallback=true and contain timebound justification.

Operator runbook snippet (what oncall does when an incident mentions residency violation)
1) Pager: if an alert fires with error code RESIDENCY_VIOLATION, immediately:
   - Pull last 30 min of traces for orgID; filter for node.region mismatches.
   - Check scheduler logs for recent node tag changes or mis-assigned placements.
2) Mitigation: triage whether this is routing misconfig, stale cache, or provisioning gap. If gating rule misapplied, flip routing rule to quarantine and reassign traffic to region-pool.
3) Communication: notify customer ops lead + legal and attach preliminary audit file.
4) Post-mortem: collect evidence package (audit CSVs, trace IDs, operator actions) and start legal review.

Telemetry and audit evidence format (minimal required fields)
- audit_report.csv columns: timestamp, org_id, request_id, node_id, node_region, storage_uri, storage_region, action (read/write), operator_id (nullable), justification (nullable), evidence_id
- retention: signed snapshot retained 1 year by default for enterprise customers; retention policy tied to contract clause.

Sample contract-ready clause (draft language for Sales/Legal to propose)
- "Redwood shall store and process Customer Data solely within the geographic region(s) specified on the Order Form (the \"Designated Region(s)\"). Redwood will not transfer Customer Data outside the Designated Region(s) except as expressly authorized in writing by Customer. For the purposes of this clause, \"Customer Data\" excludes (i) aggregated/anonymous telemetry needed to operate the Service and (ii) temporary routing metadata required for request delivery, provided no payload data is persisted outside the Designated Region(s)."

Customer Q&A (common questions SEs get)
Q: Can we allow support from other regions during incidents?
A: Yes, but we require documented JIT access (timeboxed) and session recording. Legal must approve this exception and it will appear in the customer-specific audit.

Q: Can analytics be exported to a central data warehouse?
A: Not unless anonymized and explicitly permitted. Default: analytics pipeline for resident customers runs in-region and produces aggregate reports which can be pushed out if allowed by contract.

Unresolved questions (needs legal/arch sign-off)
- What exact level of metadata is permissible to cross borders? Need a short whitelist of fields (e.g., orgID, region_hint) that legal is comfortable with.
- How to handle third-party model shards hosted outside region when models are from community/open weights with no regional mirror?

Action items (owners and ETA)
- Define explicit metadata whitelist for legal review — Owner: Mariela Soto — ETA: 2025-03-01
- Implement region-scoped cache namespace and add audit_id to traces — Owner: Devon Chen — ETA: 2025-02-15 (in progress)
